Large selections and exports

Source: vignettes/exports.Rmd
exports.Rmd
library(soilhub)

soil_observations() reads data directly into R. For very large selections (a whole dataset, a continent) the hub prepares a file instead: an export. This guide shows how to size a selection, what happens when it is too large, and how to export, download and read the files. It assumes you have signed in as shown in vignette("soilhub", package = "soilhub"). The outputs were recorded from the Global Soil Data Hub API in October 2026.

The limits of the server

The server says how much it accepts in its capabilities:

limits <- soil_capabilities(soil)$limits
limits$max_sync_observations
#> [1] 1000000
limits$max_export_observations
#> [1] 10000000
  • a direct read (soil_observations()) may hold up to 1,000,000 observations (measured values);
  • an export may hold up to 10,000,000.

Size the selection first

soil_summary() counts a selection without transferring it. For WoSIS in Kenya:

kenya <- soil_summary(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", country = "KEN")
kenya$observation_count
#> [1] 46429

About 46,000 observations: well below the limit, so a direct read works. A rule of thumb: below about 200,000 observations read directly; above, use an export (it is also the way to get files for a GIS).

When a selection is too large

If you ask for too much, the server refuses and the package stops with an error that explains what to do. Here we ask for every dataset of the hub, with no filter. We use tryCatch() to keep the error in a variable instead of stopping:

result <- tryCatch(
  soil_observations(soil, max_rows = 5),
  error = function(e) e
)
class(result)[1]
#> [1] "soilhub_load_limit_error"

The error is a soilhub_load_limit_error. Its message says why and gives the way out:

cat(conditionMessage(result))
#> The selection holds more than 1,000,000 observations, above the limit of synchronous requests (1,000,000): narrow the selection (bbox, country, datasets, variables, layer, profile_type) or request an export (POST /exports).
#> To export the same selection: soil_export(soil, format = "gpkg")
#> or rerun with too_large = "export".
#> [HTTP 422, POST /query/observations, request id soilhub-20261022172750-70f03b98]

The selection holds more than a million observations. You can narrow it (an area with bbox or country, fewer datasets or variables) or export it.

Export a selection

soil_export() sends the selection to the server, waits while the file is written, downloads it and unzips it in a folder (dir). Here: WoSIS around Vancouver (Canada) as CSV, checked every 2 seconds, saved in a temporary folder (use your own folder, for example dir = "exports").

vancouver <- c(-123.3, 49.0, -122.9, 49.4)
e <- soil_export(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", bbox = vancouver,
                 format = "csv", poll = 2, dir = tempdir())
e
#> <soil_export> exp_20261020_064345_9c0b4cf2
#>   Status:   completed (100%)
#>   Export:   format csv, content all, layout wide
#>   Selection: datasets wosis_points; bbox -123.3, 49, -122.9, 49.4
#>   Selected: 30 observations
#>   Written:  4 features, 12 observation rows, 30 observations
#>   Expires:  2026-10-27 06:43:45 UTC
#>   Zip:      /tmp/RtmpHIHIV0/exp_20261020_064345_9c0b4cf2.zip
#>   Dir:      /tmp/RtmpHIHIV0/exp_20261020_064345_9c0b4cf2
#>   Files:    features.csv, metadata.json, observations.csv
#>   Read with soil_export_read(x); cite with soil_citations(x).

The export is completed. It holds 4 features (profile sites) and 12 horizon rows, with 30 observations, in three files: the places (features.csv), the measurements (observations.csv) and a description (metadata.json). The job id (exp_...) identifies the export; the file stays on the server for a week (Expires).

Read the files back

soil_export_read() reads the measurements into a table, with the same columns as soil_observations():

horizons <- soil_export_read(e)
nrow(horizons)
#> [1] 12
horizons[, c("horizon_name", "upper_depth_cm", "lower_depth_cm", "organic_carbon")]
#> # soilhub wide table: 12 horizons, 6 variables | wosis_points | view raw, layer all
#> # no API warnings (soil_warnings), typing (soil_columns), cite with soil_citations()
#>    horizon_name upper_depth_cm lower_depth_cm organic_carbon
#> 1             F              0              1          410.0
#> 2            Ae              1              2           80.0
#> 3            Bf              2             17           80.0
#> 4             F              0              1          412.0
#> 5            Ae              1              2           83.7
#> 6            Bf              2             17           79.8
#> 7             R             17            101            0.0
#> 8            Ap              0             20           20.3
#> 9            Bg             20             38            5.2
#> 10           Bc             38             53            4.6
#> # ... 2 more row(s)

Unlike the direct read of the other guides (limited to 5 rows), the export holds every horizon of the selection: 12 horizons of 3 profiles.

The places are read with what = "features":

places <- soil_export_read(e, what = "features")
nrow(places)
#> [1] 4

Four places but only three profiles with horizons: one site has no measurements (see vignette("first-layer", package = "soilhub")).

As for any read, soil_citations() tells you what to cite:

soil_citations(horizons)$citation_text
#> [1] "Batjes NH, Calisto L and de Sousa LM, 2024. WoSIS-latest: Standardised world soil profile data. ISRIC Soil Data Hub resource identifier: https://tinyurl.com/39xhaa9d. Date downloaded: 15/01/2024."

Export now, download later

A large export can take minutes. With wait = FALSE the function returns at once; keep the job id, it is the only way to find the export again (these calls are not run here).

e <- soil_export(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", country = "BRA",
                 format = "gpkg", wait = FALSE)
e$job_id
#> [1] "exp_20261020_..."

Later, even in another R session:

e <- soil_export_wait(soil, "exp_20261020_...")
e <- soil_export_download(soil, e, dir = "exports")
horizons <- soil_export_read(e)

Files for a GIS

The formats are "csv", "tsv", "geojson", "gpkg" (GeoPackage) and "shp" (Shapefile, only for the places: content = "features"). The GeoPackage and Shapefile need the package sf to be read in R, and open directly in QGIS or ArcGIS (these calls are not run here):

gpkg <- soil_export(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", country = "KEN",
                    format = "gpkg", dir = "exports")

shp <- soil_export(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", country = "KEN",
                   format = "shp", content = "features", dir = "exports")

Let the package switch to an export

With too_large = "export" a read that the server refuses as too large is exported, downloaded and read back for you, with the same result as a direct read (this call is not run here):

x <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", too_large = "export")

If you already have the error, soil_export_from_error() exports the same selection:

e <- soil_export_from_error(soil, result, format = "gpkg", dir = "exports")
